question: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg increases diuresis because:

options.opb: Decreases the peritubular reabsorption of water.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> increases hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus -> enhances glomerular filtration rate -> increases urine production -> increases diuresis -> 80%
CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> leads to constriction of the efferent arteriole -> increases glomerular filtration rate -> promotes diuresis -> 75%

CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> causes dilation of the afferent arteriole -> increases glomerular perfusion pressure -> enhances glomerular filtration rate -> promotes diuresis -> 70%
enhanced_information: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg leads to enhanced glomerular filtration rate due to increased hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus, promoting diuresis. This is supported by the constriction of the efferent arteriole, which further increases glomerular filtration rate and diuresis. The dilation of the afferent arteriole also contributes to increased glomerular perfusion pressure and filtration rate. The evidence paths confirm the relationship between blood pressure changes and glomerular filtration rate, supporting the mechanisms of diuresis.
analysis: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg would likely lead to a decrease in diuresis due to increased reabsorption of water in the peritubular capillaries. This is a common physiological response to maintain fluid balance in the body.
